Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size a trial and (if needed) a Dedicated configuration: 

Recap of your targets and constraints (please correct if I mis-stated):
- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency <= 150 ms
- Typical request body: ~250 tokens / median response ~180 tokens
- Expected sustained throughput: ~500 req/s
- Peak concurrency: ~250 parallel requests (spiky bursts up to ~400 for <5 minutes)
- Streaming: Yes — you need partial token streaming (SSE or chunked responses) for UX
- Connection pattern: connection pooling from backend fleet; keepalives enabled; client-side pool size ~100

Questions for your team (helps us propose concrete quota/architecture):
1) Can you share a 24-hour traffic profile (CSV) with per-minute RPS and % streaming vs non-streaming?
2) Are there hard SLA/uptime constraints for this phase, or is the goal primarily to validate performance?
3) Procurement timeline and any required paperwork (PO, SOC2 evidence, security questionnaire point of contact)

Attached: acme-performance-slo-draft.xlsx — I filled in the SLO worksheet based on what we discussed.

Next steps I'm proposing:
- Vivek and our infra team will validate capacity feasibility for the numbers above and propose a short-term hosted quota increase vs a Dedicated capacity recommendation.
- I'll send a draft Mutual Action plan and a Dedicated capacity ballpark quote for your procurement team.
- Schedule a follow-up to review the trial config and any security docs (how does 30 min on Wed 6/16 10am PT look?).

If anything above looks off, say so and we'll adjust.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — this matches our notes closely. A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirm p95 target = 150ms (generation only) — we can tolerate slightly higher end-to-end if network adds latency, but generation should be tight.
- Payload: average request ~250 tokens, responses often streamed (we stream first token within ~40ms).
- Throughput: sustained ~500 req/s with spikes to 1,000 req/s for short windows.
- Concurrency: our backend maintains connection pools; we'd expect ~250 concurrent active requests, occasionally up to ~400 for <5 minutes during launch spikes.

Procurement: we need a short-term hosted option while procurement reviews a Dedicated commitment. Can Redwood lift hosted rate limits to 1,000 rps and 300-500 concurrency for a 2–4 week trial? If not, can you propose a fallback (burst token/queue) or propose a Dedicated trial?

I'll pull the traffic CSV and share it by end of day tomorrow. Procurement (procurement@acme.io) will need a ballpark cost and any SOC2/ISO evidence you can share.

Hi Sam — quick technical notes from our infra/SE side: 

1) Hosted defaults and limits (public): by default our hosted API enforces per-key rate limits to protect multi-tenant capacity. Typical soft limits are ~300 rps and ~100 concurrent in-flight requests per API key; we have escalation paths for short trials.

2) For your requested profile (500 sustained, spikes to 1k, concurrency 250–400):
- Short-term hosted: we can often grant a temporary quota increase to ~1k rps and 300 concurrency for a short trial (requires a committed start date and brief payment arrangement). This is not SLA-backed and subject to capacity.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools give predictable throughput and higher concurrency guarantees with an SLA. We would size based on model, sequence length, and streaming overhead.

3) Technical recommendations to reduce effective concurrency/cost:
- Connection pooling: set backend pool size to 100–150 and enable keepalives; use HTTP/2 multiplexing where possible.
- Batching & caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, and our intelligent batching on the runtime can reduce per-token latency under load.
- Streaming: streaming incurs more CPU and memory overhead per connection — account for ~10–20% additional capacity compared to non-streaming requests.

I'll run a sizing pass against the traffic CSV when you share it and attach a draft Dedicated quote for your procurement team (redwood-dedicated-quote.pdf).

Action items:
- Sam: share traffic CSV and any model details (model family, quantization, avg token lengths)
- Marissa: I'll need procurement contact and requested trial window to lock a hosted quota increase.

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
